items.title: What are the Vedas?
items.explanation: The Vedas are the four most ancient texts of India: the Ṛig Veda, Yajur Veda, Sāma Veda, and Atharva Veda. They consist of thousands of hymns (prayers) composed in Sanskrit, recited orally rather than written. These texts were created by rishis (male seers) and rishikas (female seers) around 1500 BCE in the Sapta Sindhava region.

items.title: Understanding Vedic Worldview
items.explanation: The Vedas express a worldview where 'Truth' is often synonymous with God. They emphasize that the Existent (Supreme Reality) is one, while sages give it many names. This unity is expressed through the mantra: 'ekam sat viprā bahudhā vadanti' (One is there, but many are called). The Vedas call for unity among people and harmony in the cosmos.

items.title: Vedic Society Structure
items.explanation: Early Vedic society was organized into 'janas' or clans—larger groups of people associated with specific regions like the Bharatas, Purus, Kurus, Yadus, and Turvaśhas. These clans shared a common purpose and spoke together, emphasizing that thoughts should agree and hearts be united.
